description: Absorption cross-sections of the absorbers the client draws, on vacuum wavelengths (rendering plan R08, R08.T4.b and R08.T4.c), written by apps/hyperion/scripts/atmosphereData.mjs cross-sections from the fetched sources named here, which are not committed. Each table's rows are [nm, sigma at each of temperaturesK]: m2 a molecule in tables, and m5 a molecule pair in pairs, whose absorption coefficient is sigma n_A n_B. Reduced values; the citations are in NOTICE's Data section.

tables.terms: The data page states no terms: reduced values with their citation, the raw table not committed (decisions-r05.md item 4)
tables.reduction: Each row is the mean of the source's 0.01 nm rows (vacuum wavelengths) over [nm - 0.5, nm + 0.5), converted from cm2 to m2 and written to 6 significant figures. A mean below zero, the source's noise near 380 nm (one, at 382 nm and 193 K), is written as 0.

tables.source: E. Karkoschka and M. G. Tomasko, Methane absorption coefficients for the jovian planets from laboratory, Huygens, and HST data, Icarus 205 (2010) 674-694, DOI 10.1016/j.icarus.2009.07.044, as converted to cross-sections by NASA's Planetary Spectrum Generator (G. L. Villanueva et al., J. Quant. Spectrosc. Radiat. Transfer 217 (2018) 86-104; https://psg.gsfc.nasa.gov)
tables.terms: The file states no terms: reduced values with their citation, the raw file not committed (decision-r08-licences.md row 1)
tables.reduction: Karkoschka and Tomasko's rows, on air wavelengths in PSG's file, are put on vacuum wavelengths 1e7/nu nm, nu each row's wavenumber on their 5 and 25 cm-1 sampling (Edlen 1966's standard air), and interpolated linearly in wavelength onto the 0.25 nm grid, finer than their 10 and 50 cm-1 spectral widths, so that no value is averaged; converted from cm2 to m2 and written to 6 significant figures. Below their first row, 25000 cm-1 (400 nm), sigma is 0: their table starts there, and Karkoschka 1998's coefficients (PDS GBAT_0001, DOI 10.17189/2bp8-k793) are 0 from 300 to 400.8 nm. The infinite-pressure coefficients, without their finite-pressure correction (their Eqs. 2-4). Between the temperatures ln sigma is the quadratic through the three, their Eq. 8 (as Collins et al. 2018, Sci. Adv. 4, eaas9593, restate it), measured over 50-300 K, the span of the k-tables their Table 4's caption names.

pairs.reduction: The file's sets on vacuum wavelengths 1e7/nu. Each 1 nm bin, [nm - 0.5, nm + 0.5), takes the first of references 54 (Finkenzeller and Volkamer 2022, 297-500 nm at 223, 263 and 293 K, with reference 32's 203 K set below them), 32 (Thalman and Volkamer 2013, 335-654 nm at 203-293 K), 30 (Spiering et al. 2011, the B band's, 671-704 nm at 293 K) and 4 (Tran et al. 2006, the A band's, 723-794 nm at 296 K) with a set covering it whole: at each of those sets' temperatures the mean of its points in the bin, linear in T between them and held beyond, converted from cm5 to m5 and written to 6 significant figures. A bin no set covers (654-671, 704-723 and 794-800 nm) is 0, and a mean below zero, the measurements' noise, is written as 0. Measured over 203-287 K, where every double-transition bin lies between two of the measurements' sets; the B and A bands' single temperatures are held at every temperature.

pairs.reduction: The file's sets at the table's 26 temperatures, on vacuum wavelengths 1e7/nu: each 1 nm bin, [nm - 0.5, nm + 0.5), the mean of a set's points in it, converted from cm5 to m5 and written to 6 significant figures. The file ends at 20000 cm-1, so the bins up to 500 nm are 0: it holds nothing shorter. ln sigma is linear in T between the temperatures, within 5% of every other set but at the file's own steps (1800-1825, 600-625 and 6000-6025 K, to 11%); measured over 200-9900 K. The sets of 950-1175 K are skipped: each lies a median 14-29% (at most 59%) below the ln-linear bridge between the 900 and 1200 K sets and falls with T in 18-100% of the bins, where every other set departs from its neighbours' trend by at most 0.3% (median) and falls in at most 5%; the 925 K set lies on the bridge and is kept.

pairs.reduction: Borysow's coefficients k, cm-1 amagat-2, for hydrogen in thermal equilibrium, as sigma = k / n0^2 with her amagat n0 = 2.68676e19 cm-3 (her 2002 paper's footnote 1), converted from cm5 to m5: each 1 nm bin, [nm - 0.5, nm + 0.5) on vacuum wavelengths 1e7/nu, the mean over its wavenumbers of the table's values interpolated linearly in wavenumber, where the table covers the whole bin, written to 6 significant figures; every other bin is 0. The 2002 tables give 60-1000 K and the 2001 table the temperatures above (its 1000 K set is not used). They end at 16490 cm-1 (60-350 K), 17000 cm-1 (400-1000 K; 16790 cm-1 at 600 K) and 20000 cm-1 (2000-7000 K), so sigma is 0 below 607, 589 (597 at 600 K) and 501 nm: the 5-0 overtone near 541 nm is untabulated below 1000 K, a stated approximation. ln sigma is linear in T between the temperatures; measured over 60-7000 K.
